## Self-host GBrain

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host; the rest of this guide installs it on the user's machine. Default to adding keyless memory to their existing agent, preserving identity and unrelated configuration. API keys, enrichment, automatic capture, and a new personal-agent identity are separate choices. The [conversation archive](docs/guides/conversation-archive.md) is on by default on a personal brain (nothing leaves a keyless machine); relay it with the first-run settings, and `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off.

> **Choose the installation path first.** Inside **[Grok Bot](docs/guides/grok-bot.md)** or **[Muse](docs/guides/muse.md)**, use their dedicated guide: the recommended shape keeps the brain on the user's own computer, published with `gbrain mcp expose --funnel` ([remote MCP](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)), and installs the thin CLI inside the agent; `scripts/setup-in-agent.sh` is the in-agent alternative, and its receipt tracks repair and native enablement. To make a brain on this computer reachable from the user's other devices, apps, or cloud agents over MCP, follow the **[remote MCP guide](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)** (`gbrain mcp expose`; confirm the plan before installing Tailscale or a service; `--funnel` only for cloud agents). For an **[existing hosted brain](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md)**, choose the harness's native OAuth/PKCE flow or a private machine handoff. Owner login, client management, permissions, and revocation use the separate [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md) path. This guide covers a local brain for other existing agents.

Usage: gbrain setup claude-code [flags]

Resolves the brain, source, transport, launcher and registration owner first and
prints them; refuses before writing anything when another owner holds the target.

config and verifies them with the harness_wiring smoke. Codex: [mcp_servers.<name>]
and the hook trust entries in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, the hooks in hooks.json.

Flags:
  --dry-run            Print the target and every step; write nothing.
  --json               One JSON document on stdout (target, decisions, steps, states).
  --surface S          MCP tool surface: verbs, starter or full, listed in full (default:
                       GBRAIN_SURFACE, then the surface already registered, then starter
                       with only the memory verbs and request_tools listed:
                       serve --surface starter --advertise verbs; full is the opt-in for
                       every operation).

  --capture            Accept automatic capture: also install the capture hooks
                       (Claude Code: Stop and SessionEnd; Codex: SessionEnd).
  --no-capture         Decline automatic capture (the default).
  --providers          Accept provider use: a new brain is created with embeddings.
  --no-providers       Decline provider use (the default: keyless, no paid calls).
  --name NAME          MCP server name (default gbrain); one name per install.
  --source ID          Pin the source the MCP server and hooks use.
  --gbrain-bin PATH    Absolute gbrain launcher (default: the gbrain on PATH).
  --serves one|several Whom the brain serves (default one: nothing changes). several labels each

{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
16|```
17|
18|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
19|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
20|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
21|operation.
22|
23|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
24|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
25|
26|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
27|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
28|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
29|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
30|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
31|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
32|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
33|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
34|  all tools enabled.
35|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
36|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
37|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
38|
39|## Brain-first instructions
40|
41|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
42|brain nobody told them about, so finish the install with:
43|
44|```bash
45|gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only
46|```
47|
48|It writes one short marked block into `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` (default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`), after your identity
49|text, which stays first and unchanged: before answering any turn,
50|search the brain first, read the best hit, fill gaps with other tools, apply your own
51|access rules, then finish the task. Text outside the markers is never touched, a
52|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
53|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
54|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never
55|creates `SOUL.md`: Hermes uses a non-empty one instead of its default identity,
56|so start Hermes once (it seeds the file) or write your identity there first.
57|
58|The same rule also rides every turn. Setup appends a marked `pre_llm_call` shell
59|hook to `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and records its approval in Hermes's
60|`shell-hooks-allowlist.json` for that exact command:
61|
62|```yaml
63|hooks:
64|  pre_llm_call:
65|    - command: "/bin/echo '{\"context\":\"GBrain: before answering this turn, check GBrain first ...\"}'"
66|      timeout: 10
67|```
68|
69|The command is self-contained: it echoes the rule as Hermes's `{"context": ...}`
70|wire shape, starts no gbrain process and needs no path on the Hermes host but
71|`/bin/echo`. Hermes appends that context to each user message, so the rule
72|reaches the model next to the turn instead of only in the system prompt. Text
73|outside the markers is never touched, and a re-run after an upgrade rewrites the
74|command and moves its approval. When config.yaml already has a `hooks:` section,
75|setup prints the entry to add yourself instead; approve it when Hermes asks (or
76|set `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`). `hermes hooks doctor` checks it: setup runs it
77|when `hermes` is on PATH and exits non-zero with `turn_hook_not_loaded` when the
78|hook is not healthy ([repair](../guides/repair.md#turn-hook-not-loaded)).
79|`--no-instructions` and `--remove` take the hook and its approval out.
80|
81|Hermes lists gbrain's tools only inside `tool_search`'s description, so with an
82|MCP connection the rule also names them (`mcp__gbrain__recall`, `mcp__gbrain__entity`
83|and the rest) and says to find them with `tool_search`.
84|
85|Search results also carry `_meta.brain_hot_memory`, the brain's recent facts.
86|Hermes may pass them to the model; they can include other sessions' facts, so
87|see [the channel's contract](../protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory)
88|before relying on them.
89|

import json, subprocess, os, sys
env = dict(os.environ, GBRAIN_HOME="/harness-state", PATH="/harness-state/.bun/bin:" + os.environ["PATH"])
p = subprocess.Popen(["/harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain", "serve", "--surface", "starter", "--advertise", "verbs"],
                     stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=env, text=True, cwd="/harness-state")
n = 0
def rpc(method, params=None, notify=False):
    global n
    msg = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
    if params is not None: msg["params"] = params
    if not notify:
        n += 1; msg["id"] = n
    p.stdin.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n"); p.stdin.flush()
    if notify: return None
    while True:
        line = p.stdout.readline()
        if not line: raise SystemExit("server closed")
        try: r = json.loads(line)
        except Exception: continue
        if r.get("id") == n: return r
def call(name, args):
    r = rpc("tools/call", {"name": name, "arguments": args})
    if "error" in r: return {"rpc_error": r["error"]}
    txt = "".join(c.get("text", "") for c in r["result"].get("content", []))
    try: return json.loads(txt)
    except Exception: return {"text": txt, "isError": r["result"].get("isError")}

init = rpc("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "hermes-verify", "version": "1"}})
print("server:", init["result"]["serverInfo"])
rpc("notifications/initialized", notify=True)
tools = [t["name"] for t in rpc("tools/list")["result"]["tools"]]
print("tools:", tools)
fact = "Install-check note: the Hermes MCP round trip for GBrain uses the keyword zephyrquartz."
rem = call("remember", {"fact": fact, "entity": "gbrain-install-check", "provenance": "install-check (Hermes MCP verify)", "content_origin": "inferred"})
print("remember:", rem.get("status"), "id", rem.get("id"), rem.get("entity_slug"), rem.get("rpc_error") or "")
rec = call("recall", {"entity": "gbrain-install-check"})
print("recall entity:", [ (f["id"], f["fact"]) for f in rec.get("facts", []) ] or rec)
kq = call("recall", {"query": "zephyrquartz"})
print("recall query keys:", list(kq.keys()))
print("recall query hit:", "zephyrquartz" in json.dumps(kq))
p.stdin.close(); p.terminate()
